title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
claims: Defines 50%-task-completion time horizon using skilled-human task duration and evaluated task-suite success rates.
Discusses external-validity limits; horizon is not agent wall-clock duration or a universal real-world automation claim.
notes: Method/result source. Its task, model and harness outcomes do not measure a local Pi/Splyce deployment.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
claims: Varies relevant-information position in multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval.
Reports position-sensitive long-context use in evaluated models.
notes: Controlled retrieval/QA evidence, not a transfer claim for every model, codebase, summary, or retrieval architecture.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
claims: Organizes observed failures into specification/system design, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification/termination categories.
notes: Trace taxonomy; it does not establish that multi-agent designs always underperform or predict Pi behavior.

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
claims: Evaluates a purpose-built agent-computer interface for repository navigation, editing and command use.
Attributes evaluated software-engineering performance in part to interface design.
notes: Benchmark/harness evidence, not a claim that the interface transfers to Pi or acts as a security boundary.

title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
claims: Evaluates a localization, repair and patch-validation pipeline without model-directed tool loops.
Documents problematic SWE-bench Lite instances and introduces a filtered comparison variant.
notes: Benchmark-specific baseline; not evidence that a static pipeline replaces exploratory or user-specific agent work. Source repository is MIT but any code reuse requires revision and dependency pinning.

title: A shared playbook for trustworthy third party evaluations
claims: Identifies harness, scorer, tool/browsing contamination, broken-task and shortcut hazards in evaluations.
Recommends making checks for these hazards visible in evaluation reports.
notes: Guidance is not a demonstrated Splyce verifier or a proof of semantic correctness for arbitrary repositories.

title: Harness engineering
claims: Describes repository knowledge and executable constraints as coding-agent engineering mechanisms.
notes: Engineering account, not controlled evidence that a particular instruction, index, or lifecycle design improves every task.

tool: Anthropic agent evaluation and long-running harness guidance
title: Agent evaluations
claims: Distinguishes isolated trials, graders and final-environment outcomes.
Supports making task quality observable; paired long-running-harness guidance separates generation and evaluation responsibilities.
notes: See also https://www.anthropic.com/research/harness-design-long-running-apps. Neither source demonstrates a Splyce supervisor or cancellation mechanism.
